doc.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Political science degree, Allstate and Stanford business fellowship
summary: After a political science degree he worked for Allstate Insurance as a personnel interviewer, then won a fellowship to Stanford business school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And you got a degree in sociology?
Political science. Decided not to pursue a career in that at that time?

No actually I first took a job for two years as a personnel interviewer, management trainee for Allstate Insurance Company. I worked in two regional offices actually, and I was also like the Affirmative Action officer for the two regions. And I was also a personnel interviewer. So I was a personnel grunt for them and in the management rotational program, which was very interesting, and you know, a Chicago based company. Northbrook, Illinois. Sears & Roebuck, at least at that time they were definitely all totally owned by Sears. I don’t know where they are now, I mean in terms of being owned. But it was very interesting. It was my first job out of college and I did it for two years and then I decided that I wanted to take advantage of an opportunity of — I was living in downtown Palo Alto, California, and my wife was working at Stanford — my first wife was working at Stanford in the sociology department. Actually she was the secretary to the head of the sociology department. And so I found out about an opportunity of a fellowship for the Stanford Business School and so I applied and, you know you take your GREs and all that sort of stuff. So anyway, I won a fellowship, the Council on Graduate Management Education for two years of study, the two year program, the MBA program at Stanford. And so I went for one year. They were paying everything — tuition, food stipend, rent, books, everything. I mean all I had to do was go to school for two years. And I was very unhappy with my colleagues. The time was 1970 so we had a lot of Vietnam Navy pilots especially coming back. And they were coming into the classes. There were a lot of them too. And my father was a Vietnam veteran also.
